  • Interfaces
    Class
    Description
    Applicative<F>
    A Functor that can lift plain values and combine independent Fs.
    ApplicativeError<F,E>
    An Applicative that can fail with an E and recover.
    Async<F>
    Can wait for a callback-based computation, such as a client library's completion handler.
    Bracket<F,E>
    A MonadError that can guarantee clean-up: acquire, use, release whatever happens.
    Concurrent<F>
    Can run Fs at the same time: start fibers, race them, run them in parallel.
    ConcurrentEffect<F>
    An effect that is both Concurrent and Effect: it can be run, and what runs can start fibers, race and run in parallel.
    Effect<F>
    An Async effect that can also be run: the top of the ladder for code that is handed an F and has to produce a value, such as a server running a request's F<Response> on that request's virtual thread.
    Fiber<F,A>
    A running F started with Concurrent.start(Kind): wait for it or cancel it.
    Foldable<F>
    Can reduce the values inside an F to one value, left to right.
    Functor<F>
    Can transform the values inside an F: the bottom of the capability ladder.
    FunctorFilter<F>
    A Functor that can drop values: what guard(...) in a comprehension needs.
    Monad<F>
    An Applicative whose next step can depend on the previous result: what forj comprehensions need.
    MonadError<F,E>
    A Monad that can fail with an E.
    Monoid<A>
    A Semigroup with an identity: combine(empty(), a) is a.
    Semigroup<A>
    A way to combine two As into one; must be associative.
    Sync<F>
    Can suspend side effects: delay(() -> println(...)) describes the print, doesn't do it.
    Traverse<F>
    A Functor and Foldable whose values can be visited with an effect, collecting the results.
